reasons: Direction is correct for our side: Corio is the licensee/customer here, and the deleted carve-out ('unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One in which case Commerce One will retain all ownership rights') would have transferred title in IP that Corio creates and funds to the vendor — the rule's walk-away item.

The redline is a clean, minimal deletion: p0115 now ends 'shall be owned by Corio.' and the orphaned continuation words at the start of p0116 are removed so the sentence reads correctly; the Commerce One assignment to Corio, the vendor's pre-existing ownership carve-in, and the NDA/invention covenants are all preserved.

The failing 'minimal edit' checks are heuristic artifacts of a whole-paragraph replace operation; a substantive diff shows only the offending carve-out (and its continuation) was struck, so the edit is in fact the smallest one that reaches the playbook position.

Comment is accurate, correctly cites the playbook position (we own what we create and fund; vendor keeps pre-existing materials), and offers a sensible fallback (support-purpose licence back to Commerce One) in the required tone with the [Playbook] prefix.

Omission of a Customer Data ownership sentence is justified — this hosting/reseller agreement contains no Customer Data concept between these two parties; leaving the 'ownership of enhancements to the Software to be negotiated' sentence intact is defensible since it creates no joint ownership and concerns derivative works of Commerce One's licensed Software.
